subject: Benchmarking cadence & ramp checks for StraitPay onboarding
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@straitpay.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam@straitpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Benchmarking cadence & ramp checks for StraitPay onboarding

Hi Elena / Liam,

Good to be working with you on the StraitPay onboarding. Per our kickoff, we want to align on a short, repeatable benchmarking cadence and the acceptance checks we'll use to sign off performance. I attached a first-pass load plan (straitpay-loadplan-v1.csv) — please review.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm the target production-like TPS and the typical request size distribution (tokens per request).
- Share a representative sample of production payloads (PII scrubbed) or a synthetic generator we can use.
- Confirm a 2-hour window where you can tolerate load testing (we prefer low-traffic overnight windows; list two options).

Suggested acceptance checks (we'll formalize in the SLO matrix):
- P95 generation latency <= 200ms for standard inference path at sustained TPS.
- P99 tail latency check during 10% prefailure bursts (spikes).
- Throughput sustained plateau for at least 15 minutes at target TPS without increased error rate.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm targets + attach sample payloads.
2) Ben / Monica and I schedule a live run where we collect traces + aggregated token latencies.
3) We share a single artifact bundle (logs + run summary) and an SLO matrix for your sign-off.

If that works, please reply with your preferred window and the sample payload link.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: straitpay-loadplan-v1.csv (CSV, 3KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena@straitpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Benchmarking cadence & ramp checks for StraitPay onboarding

Quick technical notes / questions on the load plan:

- Ramp profile: recommend a 5-minute linear ramp to 50% of target, 10-minute linear to target, 15-minute plateau, then a 10-minute spike to +30% for tail observations.
- Concurrency: we'll use the Redwood harness with continuous batching disabled for one run (to measure pure per-request latency) and enabled for a second run (to measure cost-optimized throughput).
- Cache warmup: add a 20-minute pre-warm phase at ~20% TPS to stabilize KV cache and model weights.

I'll prepare the harness config and attach it to the run artifacts. If StraitPay has a preferred header or auth token pattern, let us know so we can mirror it in request generation.

Ben
Sr. Onboarding Engineer, Redwood

Attachment: test-harness-config.json (referenced; will upload after alignment)
From: Elena Park <elena@straitpay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@straitpay.com
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Benchmarking cadence & ramp checks for StraitPay onboarding

Thanks Hannah — we reviewed the plan and can confirm an initial target of 150 TPS for our standard inference route (avg 48 tokens/request). Preliminary internal run last night gave us:
- Observed P95 ~180ms at 150 TPS (25% of requests cached)
- Error rate ~0.1% (mostly client-side timeouts we suspect)
- Noticed a warmup delta: first 10 minutes had ~30% higher p95

We can provide the sample payloads (sanitized) and grant a short SFTP window for you to pull logs. Preferred test windows:
- Thurs 18 Sep 02:00-04:00 UTC
- Fri 19 Sep 01:00-03:00 UTC

Attached are the raw logs from last night's run and a short summary (run-20250917-logs.tgz). Two asks:
1) Can Redwood validate the warmup profile and advise if KV cache warmup should be longer for our traffic?
2) We'd like a targeted tail-latency check at 5k token sequences (we spike long requests occasionally).

Elena
Principal SRE, StraitPay

Attachments: run-20250917-logs.tgz (compressed logs, 12MB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@straitpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Benchmarking cadence & ramp checks for StraitPay onboarding

Thanks Elena — great data, super helpful. We're good to take the SFTP bundle and run the two modes Ben outlined (no-batching and with-batching). Proposed schedule: run the first (no-batching) test in your Thurs 02:00-04:00 UTC window at 150 TPS with a 20-minute warmup, then run the batching-enabled test immediately after.

Action items for StraitPay:
- Please confirm we have SFTP read access for the path where run-20250917-logs.tgz lives (send credentials via the secure channel).
- Confirm the exact auth header/key used in production so we can mirror it.
- Approve the 02:00-04:00 UTC window (we'll assume yes if we don't hear back by 20:00 UTC today).

Ben / Monica — we'll collect traces and produce a short artifact bundle plus an SLO matrix for Elena to sign. Monica, can you own the result summary and SLO draft?

I'll set up the HubSpot milestone and share the Drive link after the run.

Hannah

References: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@straitpay.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Post-run: aggregated results and next steps

Elena / team — thanks for the run this morning. We completed both profiles and uploaded the artifact bundle to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/straitpay/benchmarks. Summary highlights (full SLO matrix attached: slo-matrix-straitpay.pdf):

- No-batching run (sustained 150 TPS, 15-minute plateau after warmup): P95 = 175ms, P99 = 390ms, error rate = 0.08%
- Batching-enabled run (sustained 300 TPS equivalent due to batching): P95 = 210ms (amortized), P99 = 450ms, error rate = 0.12%
- Long-sequence test (5k tokens): observed P95 = 1.9s, P99 = 2.8s — KV cache significantly reduces these when warm.

Attachments uploaded: slo-matrix-straitpay.pdf, run-20250917-logs.tgz (original), run-summary-20250918.txt.

Recommended next steps:
1) Review SLO matrix and confirm acceptance thresholds (we highlighted cells we think are negotiable).
2) If you want lower tail latency for long sequences, we can propose a cache pre-warm policy + slight autoscale cushion for those routes.
3) Upon sign-off, we'll schedule a canary rollout plan and provide the run artifact bundle for your compliance audit.

Happy to hop on a 30-min readout tomorrow. Please flag a time.

Monica Patel
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-matrix-straitpay.pdf (2 pages), run-summary-20250918.txt (1.2KB)
